answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it can vote on trades or earn reputation. The ledger links each vote to that locked stake and slashes it when a challenge proves coordinated fraud. Creating a hundred hollow identities then requires a hundred deposits, each immobilized and at risk; the attacker pays real capital and opportunity cost, even across a tundra of disconnected accounts, while one vertex of control cannot cheaply multiply influence.
